raw_response:
I farm this the way I usually do here in Quzhou: I start from last year’s practice and only adjust a little. On 10.1 mu, I cannot gamble with yield. Wheat and maize are both money crops for me, and with well irrigation I will not let the field go dry at the key stages. I finished middle school, so I do look at input cost and timing a bit more carefully, but I still trust what has worked on my land and what I see around me. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the main fertilizer down before sowing, and then topdress nitrogen when the seedlings stand well and again around jointing if the crop looks strong enough. I will give wheat about 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu, with 4 irrigations if the season is normal. For maize after wheat, I will keep the stubble and go fast, usually light tillage or no-tillage so I do not lose moisture and miss the sowing window. Maize needs strong feeding too, but I will keep it a little below wheat on total input: about 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu, with 3 irrigations. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose grain, but I still watch every yuan, so I will not push fancy products unless I saw them work clearly on nearby fields.
